{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** Legal (in-house counsel, Customer)  
**Re:** Playbook review of Vendor's Master Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against the playbook and identified **19 findings: 13 issues (3 critical, 5 high, 5 medium) and 6 compliant provisions**. The commercial architecture is materially off-market against us in four respects.

First, **there is no indemnification section at all** — the outline jumps from Section 19 (Warranties) to Section 21 (Limitation of Liability), and no defend/indemnify/hold-harmless obligation appears anywhere, leaving dangling cross-references in §§ 9.3, 19.4, 19.5, 21.3 and 30.5. Vendor therefore owes us no IP infringement or misconduct indemnity, which is a playbook walk-away scenario. We have inserted a new Section 20.

Second, **§ 14.2 vests exclusive ownership of Deliverables we commission and pay for in Vendor** and gives us only a revocable, non-transferable licence for the Order Form term — failing both the preferred position and the fallback, and inconsistent with §§ 13.2, 13.3 and 14.3.

Third, **§ 2.1 imposes a three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights"** (USD 6,000,000 aggregate), functioning as a disguised liquidated amount equal to remaining contract value and conflicting with §§ 7.1, 12.3 and 27.3. Compounding this, **Section 9 contains no termination for convenience** despite the three-year term in § 8.1.

Fourth, the Agreement contains **a cluster of one-sided restraints on us that contradict Vendor's own acknowledgement in § 12.3**: the disclose-and-match gate in § 7.2 (de facto exclusivity and reverse MFN), the worldwide 24-month non-compete in § 12.4, and the 24-month no-hire in § 12.4.

Separately, **§ 28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction** and directly conflicts with the New York County jurisdiction clause in § 28.2, and there is **no transition assistance or Customer Data return/deletion obligation** anywhere (§ 16.5 carves Customer Data out to "Sections 11 and 15", but Section 11 does not exist and Section 15 contains no return or deletion duty).

On the positive side, the limitation of liability (§ 21), assignment and change of control (§ 24), audit rights (§ 22), auto-renewal (§ 8.2–8.3), performance warranty (§ 19) and Vendor insurance (§ 18) all meet or exceed our preferred positions and require no redline.

---

## Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Issue / position taken |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | Gap between §§ 19 and 21; cross-refs at §§ 9.3, 19.4, 19.5 (quoted), 21.3, 30.5 | No indemnity anywhere. Inserted new Section 20: Vendor defence/indemnity for third-party IP, breach of law, Vendor-caused Customer Data incidents, gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard claim procedure; procure/modify/replace/refund remedies (curing the § 9.3 reference); narrow Customer indemnity. No super-cap needed — § 21.3 already treats indemnification as an Excluded Claim. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of Deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 14.2 | Vendor owns all Deliverables; we get only a revocable, term-limited licence. Reversed ownership to Customer with Vendor assignment; Vendor Technology retained under §§ 14.3 / 13.2. §§ 14.1 and 14.4 are compliant. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Cap, mutuality and carve-outs | Compliant | § 21.1 (with §§ 21.2, 21.3, 1.5, 2.1, 18.2) | Single mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' Fees "paid or payable" and USD 1,000,000; mutual consequential-loss exclusion with restoration/notification costs confirmed direct; confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement carved out. No redline. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 (with §§ 24.2–24.4, 13.3) | Customer may assign to Affiliate or successor without consent; Vendor bound asymmetrically including change-of-control consent and competitor bar; § 24.4 removes Vendor termination/repricing on our change of control. No redline. |
| 5 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 7.2 | Disclose-and-match gate operates as de facto exclusivity with no category, duration or performance-based limit, and contradicts § 12.3. Deleted; narrow fallback (single category, 12 months, auto-termination on missed service levels) offered in comment. |
| 6 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties payable by Customer | Deviation | § 2.1 | Take-or-pay "without reduction or termination rights" is a disguised Customer-payable liquidated amount equal to remaining contract value (USD 6,000,000), conflicting with §§ 7.1, 12.3 and 27.3. Removed; confirmed no take-or-pay, penalty, LDs or early-termination amount payable by Customer, with a three-months'-Fees fallback. |
| 7 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 14.2 (cf. §§ 13.1–13.3) | Deliverable licence is revocable, non-transferable, term-limited and excludes Affiliates and contractors, conflicting with the bargain in §§ 13.2–13.3. Aligned 14.2 to perpetual, irrevocable, transferable terms extending to Affiliates and contractors. |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 (second) | Worldwide, undefined-scope non-compete for 24 months post-term covering development, marketing, sale and acquisition — past the walk-away line and contrary to § 12.3. Deleted; no replacement needed as § 12.3 preserves freedom to operate. |
| 9 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Missing | § 9 (Termination); cf. §§ 8.1, 2.1 | Cause-based rights only, against a three-year term and a take-or-pay commitment expressly excluding termination rights. Added § 9.4: Customer convenience termination on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees; no Vendor convenience right during a committed term; § 2.1 conformed. |
| 10 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22.1 (with §§ 22.2, 22.3) | Once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, off-site where practicable via independent auditor; Vendor bears cost absent >5% underpayment; no direct system access; findings are our Confidential Information. No redline. |
| 11 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 28.1 (conflicts with § 28.2) | Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction is outside the accepted list and conflicts with New York County jurisdiction in § 28.2. Replaced with New York law and New York County courts. No arbitration clause elsewhere. |
| 12 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Deviation | § 7.2 | Reverse MFN requiring us to disclose and match better third-party offers — walk-away position; contradicts § 12.3. Deleted; no Vendor-granted MFN exists elsewhere. |
| 13 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Deviation | § 2.1 | Three-year USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay without reduction or termination rights, contrary to § 12.3. Replaced with fees for Services ordered or used only; 12-month reducible true-up fallback offered. |
| 14 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 | One-sided 24-month no-hire covering all Vendor employees "regardless of how the employee applies", with no general-advertising carve-out; contradicts § 12.3. Deleted; mutual 12-month non-solicit with carve-outs offered as fallback. |
| 15 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 8.2 (with §§ 8.1, 8.3) | Twelve-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, 60-day Vendor reminder with deadline extension if not sent; uplifts capped at lesser of CPI and 3% on 90 days' notice. No redline. |
| 16 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 10.1; § 16.5 (carve-out to non-existent Section 11 and to Section 15) | No transition assistance and no Customer Data return, export or deletion-certification obligation. Inserted new § 10.3: up to 6 months' assistance at then-current rates, return in a commonly used machine-readable format within 30 days, certified deletion thereafter (fallback: 90 days' assistance, same 30-day export). |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19.1 (with §§ 19.2–19.5, 17) | Professional/workmanlike and conformity warranties; 90 days for Deliverables and full subscription term for hosted Services; malicious code and Applicable Law warranties; re-performance escalating to termination and refund, expressly non-exclusive. Disclaimer in § 19.5 limited to implied warranties. No redline. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1 (with § 18.2) | CGL USD 1M/2M, workers' compensation, employer's liability USD 1M, E&O USD 2M, cyber/privacy USD 5M, term plus one year; certificates, primary coverage, cancellation notice; insurance does not cap liability. No redline. |

---

## Walk-away items

These are at or beyond our walk-away thresholds and should be treated as conditions of signature rather than negotiating currency:

1. **Absence of any Vendor indemnity (new Section 20).** No IP infringement or misconduct indemnity anywhere in the Agreement is the playbook walk-away scenario, and §§ 9.3 and 21.3 already assume one exists.
2. **§ 2.1 take-or-pay.** A liquidated amount equal to the remaining contract value (USD 6,000,000) payable "without reduction or termination rights", including after we terminate for Vendor breach, exceeds the walk-away threshold under both the LD and MINCOMMIT rules.
3. **§ 12.4 non-compete.** A post-term non-compete exceeding 12 months with an undefined "competes with Vendor" scope is past the walk-away line.
4. **§ 7.2 reverse MFN / disclose-and-match.** An open-ended obligation to extend better third-party terms to Vendor is the walk-away position; MFN is acceptable only in our favour.
5. **§ 12.4 no-hire.** A no-hire covering all Vendor personnel for 24 months with no unsolicited-approach or general-advertising carve-out sits at the walk-away line.
6. **§ 28.1 Singapore law and exclusive Singapore venue.** Outside the accepted list and approaching the walk-away position on exclusive foreign venue; it also conflicts irreconcilably with § 28.2.

---

## Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** as marked: new Section 20 (indemnification); reversal of Deliverable ownership and licence terms in § 14.2; deletion of § 7.2 and both limbs of § 12.4; removal of the § 2.1 take-or-pay; new § 9.4 (Customer convenience termination); new § 10.3 (transition assistance and data return/deletion); and New York law and venue in § 28.1.
2. **Flag the internal inconsistencies to Vendor** as a drafting matter to accelerate agreement: § 12.3 already disclaims the exclusivity, MFN, minimum-volume and no-hire commitments that §§ 7.2 and 12.4 purport to impose; § 27.3 promises termination "without penalty" against § 2.1; § 28.1 conflicts with § 28.2; § 16.5 cross-refers to a non-existent Section 11; and §§ 9.3, 19.4, 19.5, 21.3 and 30.5 cross-refer to indemnity obligations that do not exist. § 2.2's precedence ladder does not resolve conflicts internal to the Agreement.
3. **Confirm our fallbacks** with the business before the next exchange: 12-month reducible minimum with true-up (§ 2.1); three-months'-Fees early-termination fee if a commitment is unavoidable; 90 days' transition assistance with the same 30-day export; and, if a restraint is genuinely required, a single-named-product, term-only non-compete and a mutual 12-month non-solicit with general-advertising carve-outs.
4. **Preserve the compliant clauses.** Sections 18, 19, 21, 22, 24 and 8.2–8.3 meet or exceed our positions; we should not reopen them, and we should ensure Vendor's counter-draft does not narrow the § 21.3 carve-outs, § 24.4 or the § 19.5 anti-swallowing language when it responds on indemnity.
5. **Escalate if the walk-away items are refused.** We recommend deal-team and sponsor sign-off before proceeding on any draft that retains the § 2.1 take-or-pay or omits a Vendor indemnity.

*Note: verification of these findings was skipped in this pass; conclusions are based on the drafting as recorded above and should be re-confirmed against the executed draft before signature.*"}
